```{r}
#| label: setup

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(echarts4r)
library(gt)
library(leaflet)

nz_tz <- "Pacific/Auckland"

# Main centres, ordered north to south
cities <- tribble(
  ~city,          ~latitude, ~longitude,
  "Auckland",       -36.85,   174.76,
  "Tauranga",       -37.69,   176.17,
  "Napier",         -39.49,   176.91,
  "Wellington",     -41.29,   174.78,
  "Nelson",         -41.27,   173.28,
  "Christchurch",   -43.53,   172.64,
  "Queenstown",     -45.03,   168.66,
  "Dunedin",        -45.87,   170.50
)

# WMO weather interpretation codes, as documented at https://open-meteo.com/en/docs
weather_codes <- c(
  "0" = "Clear", "1" = "Mainly clear", "2" = "Partly cloudy", "3" = "Overcast",
  "45" = "Fog", "48" = "Freezing fog",
  "51" = "Light drizzle", "53" = "Drizzle", "55" = "Heavy drizzle",
  "56" = "Light freezing drizzle", "57" = "Freezing drizzle",
  "61" = "Light rain", "63" = "Rain", "65" = "Heavy rain",
  "66" = "Light freezing rain", "67" = "Freezing rain",
  "71" = "Light snow", "73" = "Snow", "75" = "Heavy snow", "77" = "Snow grains",
  "80" = "Light showers", "81" = "Showers", "82" = "Violent showers",
  "85" = "Light snow showers", "86" = "Snow showers",
  "95" = "Thunderstorm", "96" = "Thunderstorm with hail", "99" = "Thunderstorm with heavy hail"
)

compass <- function(degrees) {
  points <- c("N", "NE", "E", "SE", "S", "SW", "W", "NW")
  points[(round(degrees / 45) %% 8) + 1]
}

high_colour <- "#eb6834"
low_colour <- "#2a78d6"
rain_colour <- "#2a78d6"

# Chart canvases don't follow the page's light/dark toggle, so axis ink is a
# mid-tone that reads on both backgrounds
axis_colour <- "#898781"
gridline_colour <- "rgba(137, 135, 129, 0.25)"

# One small chart per city, laid out in a grid that wraps on narrow screens.
# City names are HTML rather than chart titles so they follow the page theme.
small_multiples <- function(charts) {
  htmltools::div(
    class = "small-multiples",
    lapply(names(charts), function(name) {
      htmltools::div(htmltools::div(class = "small-multiple-title", name), charts[[name]])
    })
  )
}

city_chart <- function(data, y_range, group) {
  data |>
    e_charts(day, height = 220) |>
    e_grid(left = 36, right = 8, top = 32, bottom = 28) |>
    e_x_axis(
      axisLabel = list(color = axis_colour),
      axisLine = list(lineStyle = list(color = axis_colour))
    ) |>
    e_y_axis(
      min = y_range[1], max = y_range[2],
      axisLabel = list(color = axis_colour),
      splitLine = list(lineStyle = list(color = gridline_colour))
    ) |>
    e_tooltip(trigger = "axis") |>
    e_group(group)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fetch

query <- c(
  latitude = paste(cities$latitude, collapse = ","),
  longitude = paste(cities$longitude, collapse = ","),
  current = paste(
    "temperature_2m", "apparent_temperature", "relative_humidity_2m", "precipitation",
    "weather_code", "wind_speed_10m", "wind_direction_10m",
    sep = ","
  ),
  daily = paste(
    "weather_code", "temperature_2m_max", "temperature_2m_min",
    "precipitation_sum", "precipitation_probability_max",
    sep = ","
  ),
  timezone = nz_tz,
  forecast_days = 7
)

url <- paste0(
  "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?",
  paste(names(query), utils::URLencode(query, reserved = TRUE), sep = "=", collapse = "&")
)

# With several locations, Open-Meteo returns one row per location, in request order
res <- jsonlite::fromJSON(url)

current <- bind_cols(cities, res$current) |>
  mutate(
    conditions = unname(weather_codes[as.character(weather_code)]),
    wind = paste(round(wind_speed_10m), "km/h", compass(wind_direction_10m))
  )

daily <- res$daily |>
  mutate(city = cities$city) |>
  unnest(cols = -city) |>
  mutate(
    city = factor(city, levels = cities$city),
    date = as.Date(time),
    day = format(date, "%a %d"),
    conditions = unname(weather_codes[as.character(weather_code)])
  )

observed_at <- as.POSIXct(current$time[1], format = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M", tz = nz_tz)
```

Conditions as of **`r format(observed_at, "%A %d %B %Y, %H:%M")`** (NZ time). This page re-renders on a schedule, so each refresh pulls the latest forecast from [Open-Meteo](https://open-meteo.com/).

## Current conditions

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Table

```{r}
#| label: current-table

current |>
  select(
    city, conditions, temperature_2m, apparent_temperature,
    relative_humidity_2m, wind, precipitation
  ) |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(
    city = "City",
    conditions = "Conditions",
    temperature_2m = "Temp (°C)",
    apparent_temperature = "Feels like (°C)",
    relative_humidity_2m = "Humidity (%)",
    wind = "Wind",
    precipitation = "Rain (mm)"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(temperature_2m, apparent_temperature), decimals = 1) |>
  fmt_number(columns = precipitation, decimals = 1) |>
  cols_align(align = "right", columns = c(temperature_2m, apparent_temperature, relative_humidity_2m, precipitation)) |>
  tab_options(table.width = pct(100))
```

### Map

Click a city for full conditions.

```{r}
#| label: current-map

# Labels sit right of the marker, except where they would cover a neighbouring city
left_labels <- c("Nelson", "Queenstown")

add_city_markers <- function(map, data, direction) {
  map |>
    addCircleMarkers(
      data = data,
      lng = ~longitude, lat = ~latitude,
      radius = 7, color = "#ffffff", weight = 2,
      fillColor = "#333333", fillOpacity = 1,
      label = ~paste0(city, " ", round(temperature_2m), "°C"),
      labelOptions = labelOptions(
        noHide = TRUE, direction = direction, textsize = "13px",
        offset = if (direction == "left") c(-8, 0) else c(8, 0)
      ),
      popup = ~paste0(
        "<strong>", city, "</strong><br>",
        conditions, "<br>",
        sprintf("%.1f", temperature_2m), " °C (feels like ", sprintf("%.1f", apparent_temperature), " °C)<br>",
        "Humidity ", relative_humidity_2m, "%<br>",
        "Wind ", wind, "<br>",
        "Rain ", sprintf("%.1f", precipitation), " mm"
      )
    )
}

leaflet(height = 560, options = leafletOptions(zoomSnap = 0.25)) |>
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldGrayCanvas) |>
  add_city_markers(filter(current, !city %in% left_labels), "right") |>
  add_city_markers(filter(current, city %in% left_labels), "left")
```

:::

## 7-day forecast

### Daily high and low (°C)

Hover over a day to see that day's values in every city.

```{r}
#| label: temp-chart

temp_range <- c(
  floor(min(daily$temperature_2m_min) / 5) * 5,
  ceiling(max(daily$temperature_2m_max) / 5) * 5
)

temp_charts <- sapply(levels(daily$city), function(name) {
  daily |>
    filter(city == name) |>
    city_chart(temp_range, group = "temperature") |>
    e_line(temperature_2m_max, name = "High", symbolSize = 8) |>
    e_line(temperature_2m_min, name = "Low", symbolSize = 8) |>
    e_color(c(high_colour, low_colour)) |>
    e_legend(right = 0, top = 0, textStyle = list(color = axis_colour))
}, simplify = FALSE)
temp_charts[[length(temp_charts)]] <- e_connect_group(temp_charts[[length(temp_charts)]], "temperature")

small_multiples(temp_charts)
```

### Daily rainfall (mm)

```{r}
#| label: rain-chart

rain_range <- c(0, max(5, ceiling(max(daily$precipitation_sum) / 5) * 5))

rain_charts <- sapply(levels(daily$city), function(name) {
  daily |>
    filter(city == name) |>
    city_chart(rain_range, group = "rain") |>
    e_bar(
      precipitation_sum, name = "Rain",
      barWidth = "50%", itemStyle = list(borderRadius = c(4, 4, 0, 0))
    ) |>
    e_color(rain_colour) |>
    e_legend(show = FALSE)
}, simplify = FALSE)
rain_charts[[length(rain_charts)]] <- e_connect_group(rain_charts[[length(rain_charts)]], "rain")

small_multiples(rain_charts)
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Forecast table

```{r}
#| label: forecast-table

daily |>
  select(
    city, date, conditions, temperature_2m_min, temperature_2m_max,
    precipitation_sum, precipitation_probability_max
  ) |>
  group_by(city) |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(
    date = "Date",
    conditions = "Conditions",
    temperature_2m_min = "Min (°C)",
    temperature_2m_max = "Max (°C)",
    precipitation_sum = "Rain (mm)",
    precipitation_probability_max = "Chance of rain (%)"
  ) |>
  fmt_date(columns = date, date_style = "wd_m_day_year") |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(temperature_2m_min, temperature_2m_max, precipitation_sum), decimals = 1) |>
  tab_options(table.width = pct(100))
```
